questions.question_text: Find the sum of the roots of $3x^{4}+8x^{3}-2x^{2}+5x-7=0$.

options.why: Omitted the negative sign in the sum formula $\sum\alpha=-b/a$.
Calculated the pair sum $c/a=-2/3$ instead of the single sum $-b/a$.
Calculated the four-root product $e/a=-7/3$ instead of the single sum $-b/a$.

questions.question_text: For the quartic $x^{4}-5x^{3}+7x^{2}-3x+4=0$, what is the sum of the products of roots taken two at a time?

options.why: Incorrectly applied a negative sign to the pair sum $+c/a$.
Calculated the single sum of roots $-b/a$ instead of the pair sum.
Calculated the triple sum of roots $-d/a$ instead of the pair sum.
Forgot the negative sign in the formula $\sum\alpha\beta\gamma=-d/a$.
Calculated the single sum $-b/a$ instead of the triple sum.
Calculated the product of all four roots $e/a$ instead of the triple sum.

questions.question_text: What is the product of all four roots of $4x^{4}-7x^{3}+x^{2}-9x-16=0$?

options.why: Applied an unnecessary negative sign to $e/a$ for the degree-4 product.
Calculated the triple sum $-d/a$ instead of the root product.
Calculated the single sum $-b/a$ instead of the root product.

questions.question_text: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of $x^{4}-3x^{3}+2x^{2}-8x+4=0$, find the value of $\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{1}{\gamma}+\frac{1}{\delta}$.

options.why: Used an incorrect sign for the quotient $(-d/a)/(e/a)$.
Inverted the numerator and denominator of the reciprocal sum formula.
Used the single sum $-b/a$ in the numerator instead of the triple sum $-d/a$.

questions.question_text: One root of $x^{4}-5x^{3}+2x^{2}+20x-24=0$ is $2$. Find the sum and product of the other three roots.

options.why: Used the sum and product of all four roots without removing the known root $2$.
Treated the known root as $-2$, giving $5-(-2)=7$ and $-24/(-2)=12$.
Used $-e/a=24$ instead of $e/a=-24$ for the four-root product, then divided by $2$.

questions.solution_text:
Let the other three roots be $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$.
$2+\alpha+\beta+\gamma=5$
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=3$
$2\alpha\beta\gamma=-24$
$\alpha\beta\gamma=-12$

questions.question_text: For the quartic $x^{4}-4x^{3}+5x^{2}-6x+2=0$, find the value of $\sum\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}$.

options.why: Used an incorrect sign when computing the pairwise reciprocal sum.
Evaluated the reciprocal single sum instead of the pairwise reciprocal sum.
Used the four-root product in both numerator and denominator, calculating $2/2=1$ instead of $5/2$.

questions.question_text: Find the zeroes of $x^{4}-3x^{3}-28x^{2}+36x+144$ given that they are $\alpha, 2\alpha, \beta, 2\beta$.

options.why: Used $b/a=-3$ instead of $-b/a=3$ for the root sum, giving $\alpha+\beta=-1$ with $\alpha\beta=-6$.
Repeated $\alpha$ and $\beta$ instead of including the doubled roots $2\alpha$ and $2\beta$.
Incorrectly simplified $4\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}=144$ to $\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}=4$, giving $\alpha\beta=-2$ and $\alpha+\beta=1$.

questions.solution_text:
$3\alpha+3\beta=3$
$\alpha+\beta=1$
$4\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}=144$
$(\alpha\beta)^{2}=36$
$\alpha\beta=\pm6$
The pair sum is $2\alpha^{2}+9\alpha\beta+2\beta^{2}=2(\alpha+\beta)^{2}+5\alpha\beta=-28$.
$2+5\alpha\beta=-28$
$\alpha\beta=-6$
$\beta=1-\alpha$
$\alpha(1-\alpha)=-6$
$\alpha^{2}-\alpha-6=0$
$(\alpha-3)(\alpha+2)=0$
$\alpha=3$ or $\alpha=-2$, giving $\beta=-2$ or $\beta=3$ respectively.
The zeroes are $-2, -4, 3, 6$.
